origin_year_or_period.value: developed from around 1890 to the early 1900s, named and popularised in the early 1920s

conservation_status.value: not at risk worldwide (2024); listed at risk/endangered in Australia's DAD-IS and as a priority breed on the UK Rare Breeds Survival Trust watchlist; removed from the US Livestock Conservancy watchlist in 2023

value: set a world egg-laying record of 309.5 eggs per hen average over 365 days in 1922-23
derived from the British Black Orpington

history_summary.value: The Australorp was developed in Australia from imported Black Orpington stock crossed with breeds such as Rhode Island Red, Minorca, White Leghorn and Langshan to improve egg-laying utility. It became famous worldwide in the 1920s after a record-setting egg-laying trial and was added to the American Poultry Association's Standard of Perfection in 1929.
